checks.context: Without this, a single `cloudformation delete-stack` wipes out every resource in the stack. AWS Config flags this as NON_COMPLIANT. Enable it on every production stack — you can always disable it before a planned teardown.

checks.message: No service role specified — CloudFormation will use your caller credentials
checks.context: Without a dedicated service role, CloudFormation inherits your IAM permissions. This makes it hard to audit what CloudFormation did vs what you did directly, and can grant more permissions than the stack actually needs.

checks.message: Never embed credentials or secrets in template parameters
checks.context: Stack parameters are stored in plaintext in CloudFormation and visible to anyone with cloudformation:DescribeStacks. Use SSM SecureString or Secrets Manager dynamic references ({{resolve:secretsmanager:...}}) instead.

checks.message: Run a change set first — direct updates skip the review step
checks.context: Direct stack updates apply changes immediately with no preview. Change sets show you exactly what will be added, modified, or replaced (including resources that require replacement, which means deletion + recreation).

checks.message: Stack deletion destroys all resources that don't have DeletionPolicy: Retain
checks.context: RDS instances, S3 buckets, DynamoDB tables — all gone unless you've set DeletionPolicy: Retain or Snapshot. Check the template before proceeding. This is one of the most common causes of production data loss.

checks.message: Review the change set output carefully before executing — pay attention to replacements
checks.context: A 'Replacement: True' in the change set means the resource will be deleted and recreated. For stateful resources (RDS, EBS, DynamoDB) this means data loss unless DeletionPolicy is set.

checks.message: Executing a change set is irreversible once started
checks.context: Once execution begins, CloudFormation processes changes in order. If it fails mid-way, rollback may not restore everything cleanly — especially for resources with DeletionPolicy: Retain or custom resources.

checks.message: Verify the stack policy doesn't accidentally deny all updates
checks.context: A stack policy with Effect: Deny on all resources blocks every future update. This is a common mistake when copy-pasting policies. Always test with a specific resource logical ID before applying broadly.

checks.message: StackSets deploy to multiple accounts/regions simultaneously — test in one account first
checks.context: A misconfigured StackSet can simultaneously break infrastructure across dozens of accounts. Always deploy to a single test account first, verify, then expand the deployment targets.

checks.message: StackSet updates propagate to all target accounts — use deployment preferences to limit blast radius
checks.context: Without --deployment-preferences, updates roll out to all accounts at once. Set MaxConcurrentPercentage and FailureTolerancePercentage to control rollout speed and stop on failures.
